content.comment_body: Hello, I understand this is an older topic, but I'm having the same issue. Some relays remain stuck and won't release. I am using two PLCs: • [article_no] ([product_name] | DC 12/24V) • [article_no] ([product_name] | AC/DC 24V) The main issue is with the [product_name] controlling several outputs. It's being used to operate lighting, and the connected loads aren't particularly high (about 12W per circuit). What options do I have to solve this? Thank you in advance.

Hi, Refer to my reply in the related discussion. Typically, relays in [product_name] can experience inrush currents up to 30A. For LED lighting (rated at 230V AC), you should expect an inrush of approximately 3.5A per watt for quality products, and up to 4A per watt for lower quality ones. For instance, with good LED brands, a 12W circuit could draw an inrush of about 42A (3.5A/W × 12W). With lower quality LEDs, it could reach 48A (4A/W × 12W). In both scenarios, this exceeds the relay's maximum inrush rating. Consider using an inrush current limiter (search online for more information) to reduce the inrush current. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: A user reports certain relays connected to [product_name] fail to release or operate correctly when switching LED lighting loads, even with modest wattage. Another contributor identifies that high inrush currents from LED fixtures surpass the relay limits, causing these operational issues. As a solution, using an inrush current limiter is recommended.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants all relays in [product_name] to reliably switch LED loads, even at moderate wattages, without getting stuck or blocked.
